companyDescription: eVTOL Air Taxi · First manufacturer to complete FAA Type Certification Phase 3 of 4 · Acquiring Boeing's Wisk Aero, Insitu & SkyGrid (antitrust cleared Sep 2026) · $1.56B cash cushion
priceNote: Self-fetched today (live-prices.json cache dated Aug 13, too stale to use). Down 7% in the last session on rising Treasury yields hitting speculative growth broadly, but up modestly since the Jul 2 report ($4.97 → $5.18) after clearing a major new catalyst: the Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust waiting period for Archer's acquisition of Boeing's Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid subsidiaries expired Sep 18.
summary: Archer cleared a major new catalyst since the last report: the antitrust waiting period on its acquisition of Boeing's Wisk Aero (autonomous eVTOL tech), Insitu (military drones) and SkyGrid (airspace management software) expired Sep 18, with the deal expected to close by end of 2026 pending other regulatory approvals. That materially expands the thesis beyond pure FAA Type Certification into defense-adjacent, autonomy-IP territory. Cash position is $1.56B as of Q2 2026 (Aug 10) against a $263.2M quarterly net loss — real burn (up from $217.7M last quarter) but still ~5-6 quarters of runway, well clear of any survival threshold. Cathie Wood's ARK bought shares this month, funded by selling PLTR and AMD. Phase 4 FAA certification itself has no fresh confirmed timeline update since the last report, and the stock remains rate-sensitive — it just sold off 7% on rising yields.

catalysts.name: Boeing Wisk Aero / Insitu / SkyGrid Acquisition Close
catalysts.description: HSR antitrust waiting period expired Sep 18, 2026. Deal expected to close by end of 2026 pending other customary regulatory approvals. Adds autonomous eVTOL IP (Wisk), military drone manufacturing (Insitu), and airspace-management software (SkyGrid) — a genuine expansion of the moat beyond air-taxi certification alone.

catalysts.name: FAA Type Certification — Phase 4 (Final Phase)
catalysts.description: Archer remains the first eVTOL manufacturer to have completed Phase 3 of 4 in FAA Type Certification. No fresh confirmed timeline update on Phase 4 completion since the last report; still targeted for H2 2026 per prior company guidance.

catalysts.name: Commercial Readiness — 'No Roads' Flight Tour
catalysts.description: Midnight completed a piloted 40-mile Salinas-to-Hollister flight (12 minutes vs 40+ by car) and is touring multiple US states with BETA Technologies to build charging infrastructure in Texas under the White House eVTOL Integration Pilot Program.

risks: Still essentially pre-revenue — $5.0M Q2 revenue against a $263.2M quarterly net loss (burn increased from $217.7M last quarter); the thesis is still entirely about certification/commercialization timing, not current fundamentals
Stock fell 7% in the most recent session purely on rising Treasury yields — confirms this remains a high-beta, rate-sensitive name even with strong cash on hand

Wisk/Insitu/SkyGrid is a large, complex three-subsidiary acquisition still pending 'other customary closing conditions, including additional regulatory approvals' beyond the antitrust clearance — integration and remaining-approval risk is real, not yet fully de-risked
No confirmed update on FAA Phase 4 timeline since the last report — the certification clock hasn't visibly advanced even as the M&A story has
A single public eVTOL safety incident — Archer's or a competitor's — remains a standing sector-wide overhang independent of company execution

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Archer is pre-revenue and cash-burn-heavy — the stock's 7% drop on rising Treasury yields this week is direct, live evidence of rate sensitivity, even with a $1.56B cash cushion providing multi-year runway.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Aircraft manufacturing/component costs are exposed to input-cost inflation; a secondary factor versus certification/M&A-integration timing risk.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: MEDIUM-HIGH. The recent yield-driven selloff shows high-burn, pre-revenue growth names in this sector remain squarely exposed to rate moves, despite Archer's genuinely improving strategic position via the Boeing acquisition.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk MEDIUM — strong cash position buys real runway, but the stock just demonstrated live rate-sensitivity (-7% on a yields move), confirming this is still a multiple-compression risk, not just a financing-cost risk.

entryStrategy.verdict: Moonshot — 2-3% max. Measured turbo median at-catalyst return is -13.7% (n=19), so prefer the dip zone ($4.55-4.90) over chasing here. Base (Phase 4 + deal close on track) → $8.29 (+60%), Bull (certification granted) → $11.91 (+130%), Moon (certification + Boeing-deal synergies) → $17.87 (+245%). The Wisk/Insitu/SkyGrid acquisition is a genuine conviction upgrade from the pure-certification bet this was in July.

catalystSpot.preRunup: eVTOL stocks run hard on FAA certification phase-completion news — the Phase 3 milestone drove a same-day +4% move in July. Antitrust clearance on the Boeing deal (Sep 18) did not produce a similarly large single-day pop, based on available data, suggesting the market is treating the M&A story more cautiously than a pure certification win.

th.summary: Archer ผ่าน catalyst ใหม่สำคัญตั้งแต่รายงานก่อน — ระยะเวลารอ antitrust (HSR) สำหรับการซื้อ Wisk Aero (เทคโนโลยี eVTOL แบบ autonomous), Insitu (โดรนทหาร) และ SkyGrid (ซอฟต์แวร์จัดการน่านฟ้า) จาก Boeing หมดอายุ 18 ก.ย. คาดปิดดีลภายในสิ้นปี 2026 รอ regulatory approval อื่นๆ ขยาย thesis ไปไกลกว่าแค่ FAA Type Certification เข้าสู่พื้นที่ defense-adjacent และ autonomy IP งบดุลมีเงินสด $1.56B ณ Q2 2026 (10 ส.ค.) เทียบขาดทุนสุทธิรายไตรมาส $263.2M — burn จริง (เพิ่มจาก $217.7M ไตรมาสก่อน) แต่ยังมี runway ราว 5-6 ไตรมาส ไกลจาก survival threshold Cathie Wood ของ ARK ซื้อหุ้นเดือนนี้ โดยขาย PLTR และ AMD เพื่อซื้อ FAA Phase 4 เองยังไม่มีอัปเดต timeline ใหม่ตั้งแต่รายงานก่อน และหุ้นยัง rate-sensitive จริง — เพิ่งลง 7% จากดอกเบี้ยพันธบัตรขึ้น
